messages:
ash: Customer on prod reports streaming generation hangs after the first JSON chunk, then client blocks waiting for more. Happens intermittently behind Envoy + gzip. Repro included below.

ash: Minimal repro (Go):
```go
resp, err := client.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for resp.Scan() { // using sdk scanner
  chunk := resp.Token()
  fmt.Println(string(chunk))
}
if resp.Err() != nil { log.Println("stream err:", resp.Err()) }
```

ash: Logs show the scanner paused after printing first object. No error. Go SDK v0.18.1. Retries enabled via middleware.

sara: Are they using the builtin scanner (bufio.Scanner) or the decoder helper?

ash: builtin scanner from the SDK (default Stream()). I asked them to try disabling retries but they saw same behavior once.

kevin: Can you grab raw bytes from the wire (tcpdump or curl --raw) and paste hex? my hunch is Envoy is inserting a leading colon-style keepalive (": ping") or doing chunk size munging when gzip + chunked interact.

ash: pasted hex below from customer tcpdump (first 2 chunks):
```
0000: 0d0a 3a20 7069 6e67 0d0a 0d0a 7b22 746f 6b65 6e22 3a20 2261 22 0d0a
0010: 0a0c 0000 0000 000a 7b22 7365 63 22 3a20 2273 65 63 2d 32 22 7d 0d0a
```

ash: So sequence is CRLF, ": ping" CRLF CRLF, then start of JSON. Scanner seems to treat the leading CRLF as an empty token and then hang waiting for EOF.

sara: hmm. bufio.Scanner treats newlines as token terminator; if the SDK's split func expects JSON objects and sees a stray CRLF it can produce an empty token. But usually empty tokens are skipped. Could be the scanner max token size or the split function incorrectly consumes the first CRLF leaving the initial '{' in buffer expecting more bytes.

maya: I remember a regression in upstream where we changed how we handle leading comment lines for SSE-like keepalives (": ping"). We added code to strip lines starting with ':' but maybe only on the hosted path; not in the go-sdk code path. Any chance the customer is hitting the hosted variant that emits SSE-style pings?

ash: They said responses come from our hosted API via Envoy edge, yes. Host shows intermittent pings when idle.

kevin: Two actionable asks:
1) Can the customer reproduce with curl -N --raw to see raw bytes? That tells us if Envoy is emitting the ping before gzip decompress or after.
2) Try go-sdk v0.18.2-alpha (internal build) which has a change to the streaming split that tolerates leading SSE comments. If it still repros, disable response decompression in Envoy for this route to see if gzip+chunked recomposition is root cause.

ash: Customer ran curl -N --raw and pasted raw output: they still see the ": ping" line before JSON.

ash: They tested go-sdk v0.18.2-alpha and the scan still stalls ~1/3 of the runs.

sara: OK, next theory: the retry middleware may be replaying request on a connection that already returned a first chunk; partial stream replay + decoder state could cause decoder to wait for continuation. Can you confirm whether retries are happening (logs show 1xx/5xx)?

ash: They had a retry policy with max 1 retry. Logs show occasional 502 then a subsequent attempt that succeeds but the client still hung on the stream that reported success.

kevin: That matches: if the first attempt produced a keepalive + partial JSON and the retry switches connection, the SDK's scanner might be reading from the original net.Conn which was half-closed by proxy and never gets the rest. Workaround: disable automatic retries for streaming requests.

ash: I asked customer to set headers to force no-retry and retest. They confirmed disabling retries eliminated the hang in their runs so far. :thumbsup:

maya: Good. For a long-term fix we should:
- make SDK streaming split robust to leading SSE/comment lines and stray CRLFs
- ensure the retry middleware doesn't replay on partially-read response bodies (detect streaming endpoint and avoid transparent retry)

sara: Agreed. We'll prepare an SDK patch that (1) switches streaming to use a buffered reader + custom split func instead of bufio.Scanner, and (2) exposes a StreamOptions flag to opt out of transparent retries.

kevin: Also add server-side note: edge should avoid injecting SSE pings when content-type is application/json; or if we must, send them as separate SSE event frames so clients can discard safely. I'll open an eng-runtime issue to review Envoy config.

ash: infra-bot: canary mention — I saw a canary deploy around the time customer started seeing this.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout for runtime/edge v2026.03.17-rc3 completed on 3 hosts at 2026-03-17T14:02:10Z.

ash: Thanks — that correlates.

sara: I'll push a go-sdk PR today for 0.18.3 with the scanner fix and StreamOptions. Patch note will recommend disabling automatic retries until middleware is updated.

ash: Customer confirmed disabling retries as workaround, and will wait for SDK patch. I'll follow up when they test 0.18.3.

kevin: Filed ENG-1742 (edge envoy: review SSE pings + gzip/chunked interaction).

sara: Assigning to eng-runtime + go-sdk owners. ETA: 24h for SDK patch, 48-72h for runtime config review. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ash: Thanks all. Keep me posted.
